scope: T3 and T6 public ratings
statement: How should a public rating be reported when a held or unreviewed finding sets that rating?

scope: T3 and T6 public ratings
statement: Held and unreviewed findings count in synthesis. Publish the rating and label it provisional when a confirmed rating setter is held or unreviewed. If setter coverage is incomplete and no unresolved setter is confirmed, report the status as undetermined.

scope: T3 and T6 public ratings
statement: The edition status builder records unresolved setter IDs and distinguishes provisional, assessed clear and undetermined. Its held-setter replay retains the finding and rating.

scope: Evidence classification and interpretation
statement: Separate knowledge basis from extraction format and document source dependence and literature-derived expert judgement.

scope: Evidence classification and interpretation
statement: Add independent knowledge_basis and extraction_format fields. Preserve legacy claim_basis and historical analytical reproduction. Migrate table/figure labels to unknown knowledge basis without inferring measurement. New claims require independently stated basis and format. Do not infer independence from row counts or authorship. Expert opinion is derived from literature; no direct elicitation is in scope. Numerical weighting changes require a separate scientific release.

scope: Evidence classification and interpretation
statement: Additive classification migration and validated intake preserve original evidence and analytical table hashes across all six practices.

scope: T4 synthesis workflow
statement: Clarify agent-led T4 synthesis separately from historical deterministic derivation and from validation, packaging and runtime evaluation.

scope: T4 synthesis workflow
statement: New T4 mappings are to be derived by an AI agent using a versioned skill and reviewed evidence, with traceable proposals and scientific approval. Deterministic checks and packaging do not make the scientific synthesis decision. Preserve historical compiler methods only for reproduction; do not claim a new production agent run is implemented or validated. T3/T6/T6E algorithms and historical analytical outputs are unchanged.

scope: T4 synthesis workflow
statement: Retire the historical T4 compiler from current documentation and execution routes while preserving immutable historical evidence editions.

scope: T4 synthesis workflow
statement: Retain agent-led T4 proposals, traceable scientific acceptance and deterministic validation/packaging. Remove historical T4 synthesis algorithms from supported current workflows and documentation; keep immutable Git editions and existing analytical records as explicitly historical baselines. Do not relabel historical outputs as agent-generated or imply that the production agent route is implemented. The intended extension to AI-led T3/T6 requires its own versioned scientific proposal and acceptance implementation; existing effect algorithms are not silently recalibrated by T4 retirement.

scope: T3/T6 scientific synthesis and accepted-output execution
statement: Should T3/T6 scientific synthesis move from automatic scoring to AI-authored proposals with explicit scientific acceptance?

scope: T3/T6 scientific synthesis and accepted-output execution
statement: AI authors T3/T6 scientific synthesis: routing, dependence and compatibility, direction and strength, evidence level, agreement, confidence, applicability, optional numerical summaries, asset weights and rationale. Code only validates, packages and runs accepted outputs; fixed weights, rank mappings, confidence matrices and fallback ratings cannot author new science. Bind scientific acceptance to exact immutable proposal bytes and input/model/skill provenance; hold stale or unresolved outputs. Retain existing T3/T6 as historical until explicitly replaced; no retrospective AI acceptance. Retire the shared automatic effect/economic generator; T6E stays frozen pending its own contract. T4 compiler retirement remains in force. This supersedes historical provisional-setter eligibility for new outputs: included evidence must be reviewed with no unresolved hold.

scope: T3/T6 scientific synthesis and accepted-output execution
statement: Implemented native AI authoring skill, immutable input/skill and CSV proposals, authenticated scientific acceptance, stale/held-output blocking and exact accepted-output packaging in RuralScan/evidence. Runtime AcceptedEffects verifies the trusted package and reads authored values without re-rating. Existing scientific rows remain historical; no real scientific acceptance is asserted by the workflow implementation.

scope: T2/T5 classification, M3 characterisation and M4 priority aggregation
statement: Define a shared explicit problem-classification and user-weighting route for T2 climate variables and T5 priorities, and assess whether CRITIC should determine priority weights.

scope: T2/T5 classification, M3 characterisation and M4 priority aggregation
statement: Use none 0, low 0.33, medium 0.66 and high 1, threshold classes by default and explicitly referenced terciles as an alternative; no quintiles. T2 is a variable registry without a composite climate-risk index. Choose one representative per shared concern with a recorded reason. Normalize explicit nonnegative user weights once across the stack and preserve unknown positive-weight inputs. M2b remains separate. CRITIC is diagnostic only, not an automatic multiplier or replacement of user priorities. Historical CSV settings are not defaults; real variable calibration still requires scientific review.

scope: T3/T6 effect extraction: hazard-year findings with a normal-year comparison
statement: When a source reports a practice's effect in a hazard year and in normal years for the same outcome, should the hazard benefit be the hazard-year effect or its difference from the normal-year effect?

scope: T3/T6 effect extraction: hazard-year findings with a normal-year comparison
statement: Where a source reports the same practice and outcome in a hazard year and in normal years, encode two findings. The normal-year effect is the ordinary finding with no hazard tag. The hazard benefit is the hazard-year effect minus the normal-year effect, in units of the same metric (percentage points for a percent change), tagged with the hazard. This derived magnitude is a bounded exception to the verbatim-number rule. Both source figures must appear in the quote, and the finding records the calculation, which must reproduce exactly. Ranges are differenced conservatively: low = hazard low - normal high, high = hazard high - normal low. Applies to new extraction now; existing findings with normal_year_reference = present are re-coded in a targeted backfill. Hazard-year findings without a normal-year comparison keep the existing x0.7 weighting.

scope: Agroforestry FAM definitions, linear placement families and attribution preservation
statement: Clarify overlapping agroforestry variants and distinguish boundary, wind and contour placement families while preserving historical attribution, evidence IDs and human review history.

scope: Agroforestry FAM definitions, linear placement families and attribution preservation
statement: Retain planted_silvopasture and agrosilvopasture in agroforestry__silvopastoral, distinguishing a separate crop component and observed management timing. Split linear placement into agroforestry__boundary_planting, agroforestry__wind_shelter and agroforestry__contour_buffers, all applicability_zone; preserve their subpractice IDs. Retire agroforestry__linear_boundary for new assignments without aliasing it to one successor. Preserve its pinned definitions and all previous attribution. Boundary location and wind/runoff function may overlap, but a physical feature and its evidence must not be double-counted. Clarify other variants and evidence-only tags as specified in the linked decision. Existing findings require a separate source-reviewed migration PR; do not rewrite IDs, discard review or receipt history, transfer old approvals to changed scope, duplicate search protocols, or automatically re-rate outputs. Unresolved scope remains visible under its original attribution. Fresh affected AI proposals need current input hashes and human acceptance. Runtime and publication adoption are separate.

scope: Hierarchical agroforestry evidence coverage and scientific synthesis
statement: Ensure finer agroforestry practice definitions retain a route to broader family, group and practice-level evidence summaries instead of fragmenting the evidence base.

scope: Hierarchical agroforestry evidence coverage and scientific synthesis
statement: Support specific subpractice to suitability family to optional evidence group to agroforestry aggregation. Linear plantings is an evidence group above boundary planting, wind shelter and contour buffers, not a pooled suitability family or a legacy-family alias. Retain direct broader evidence at its real scope and show it when child support is sparse. Count parent evidence as a union of evidence IDs; assess independence through reviewed origins, not row counts. Compatible eligible child and broader findings can support a scope-justified AI parent synthesis with human acceptance, showing covered children, uncertainty and conflicts. A parent conclusion does not establish support for every child; missing child support is not zero. No automatic downward inheritance, copying of sibling rules, averaging of placement gates or revival of retired family-voting formulas. Source applicability and current review eligibility remain binding. Preserve IDs and review history. Group attribution, retrieval and parent-output validation must be implemented in the separate evidence-adoption PR; this method release does not claim those consumers exist.
